nodes.label: Code Review: about page and related flow
nodes.rationale: Not ready for production: 4 critical issues centred on auth-material logging, unauthenticated confirmed-user creation, and fail-open non-atomic rate limiting.

nodes.label: Code Review: Account
nodes.rationale: Not ready for production: 4 critical issues. Profiles/orders RLS exists, but sessions and audit_logs lack explicit deny-by-default policies.

nodes.label: Code Review: actions news and related flow
nodes.rationale: Not ready for production: 3 critical issues; admin news paths bypass RLS via service role and emit no audit trail.

nodes.label: Code Review: Admin Security Surface
nodes.rationale: Three-pass review (frontend/API/DB). 7 critical issues; residual risk is that admin order and KPI routes rely on service role instead of DB-enforced admin RLS.

nodes.label: Code Review: Auth Security Hardening
nodes.rationale: Reviews the security hardening change itself and finds the hardening both ineffective (rate limit no-ops) and operationally breaking (admin UI 403).

nodes.label: Code Review: Cart Security
nodes.rationale: Not ready for production: 4 critical issues around Stripe session binding, stock integrity, service-role RLS bypass and missing input validation.

nodes.label: Code Review: Checkout
nodes.rationale: PCI scope correctly reduced via Stripe Elements and webhook signature verification uses the raw body, but order finalization is not bound to an immutable snapshot.

nodes.label: Code Review: Contact
nodes.rationale: Contact inquiry bodies, names and emails are stored in audit_logs in plaintext, and the shared-token audit-log API turns that into an information disclosure path.

nodes.label: Code Review: Home Page
nodes.rationale: Security headers via proxy.ts and RLS on public content tables were confirmed; the residual gaps are logging, unpublished-item leakage through LOOK, and unthrottled search.

nodes.label: Code Review: item/[id]
nodes.rationale: 6 critical issues; the unifying cause is service-role item lookups without a status='published' predicate across cart, wishlist and checkout.

nodes.label: Code Review: Item Page
nodes.rationale: React auto-escaping removes immediate XSS risk, but public API plus public bucket leaves high scraping and pre-publication asset exposure risk.

nodes.label: Sensitive auth material written to server logs
nodes.rationale: Cookie headers and decoded token fragments are logged on ordinary requests, so any log-access compromise yields session material; fix is to log only presence booleans and request ids.

nodes.label: Service-role client bypasses RLS
nodes.rationale: Using service-role credentials on request paths disables the database guardrail, so isolation depends on every query remembering its filter; a single future query bug becomes full data exposure.

nodes.label: State-changing endpoints skip CSRF middleware
nodes.rationale: Cookie-authenticated mutations accept requests without double-submit verification, diverging from the documented auth design already applied by logout.

nodes.label: Public endpoints lack abuse throttling
nodes.rationale: Unthrottled public routes enable enumeration, scraping, expensive Stripe object creation, and amplification against upstream APIs.

nodes.label: Privileged operations emit no audit trail
nodes.rationale: Create/update/status-change/delete and role changes are untraceable, conflicting with the admin audit design and weakening incident investigation.

nodes.label: audit_logs lacks RLS and append-only integrity controls
nodes.rationale: The migration creates the table without RLS, admin-only read policies, append-only constraints or hash/integrity mechanisms, so the DB layer enforces neither least privilege nor tamper evidence.

nodes.label: OTP session tokens persisted in localStorage
nodes.rationale: Access and refresh tokens stored under supabase.auth.token can be exfiltrated by any origin XSS, enabling full impersonation; HttpOnly cookies or in-memory bearer tokens are required instead.

nodes.label: Rate limiting fails open on backend errors
nodes.rationale: DB or middleware errors let the request continue, so brute-force protection disappears exactly when the backend is degraded; sensitive auth endpoints should fail closed.

nodes.label: Rate limit counter updates are not atomic
nodes.rationale: Select-then-update/insert undercounts concurrent requests, allowing effective bypass; a single atomic upsert or DB function is required.

nodes.label: UNIQUE(ip,endpoint,bucket) with NULL ip defeats account rate limiting
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL UNIQUE does not treat NULLs as equal, so subject-scoped rows never collide and ON CONFLICT never fires; every attempt inserts count=1, nullifying login brute-force, OTP flood and reset-mail bombing defence.

nodes.label: Unauthenticated admin user creation endpoint
nodes.rationale: The route invokes service-role auth.admin.createUser with no authn/authz, so anyone reaching it can mint privileged accounts.

nodes.label: Static shared secret used instead of user-bound admin auth
nodes.rationale: x-admin-token === ADMIN_API_KEY bypasses session-bound auth, RBAC, 2FA state and actor attribution; possessing one secret is enough to read audit logs or revoke any user's sessions.

nodes.label: Broken Access Control
nodes.rationale: Umbrella defect class covering unauthenticated privileged routes, over-broad refund permission, token-role authorization and RLS bypass findings across the 2026-04-18 review set.

nodes.label: Refund authorization broader than the spec
nodes.rationale: admin.orders.manage is granted to supporter by legacyPermissionMap, so a supporter can issue Stripe refunds although the spec restricts refunds to admin; needs an admin-only check or a dedicated admin.orders.refund permission.

nodes.label: Token role treated as authorization source in hybrid RBAC
nodes.rationale: Granting when either DB ACL or legacyPermissionMap[tokenRole] allows means stale app_metadata.role survives DB revocation, breaking the documented 'DB ACL as authority' model.

nodes.label: Admin 2FA/MFA state not enforced at auth gates
nodes.rationale: Admin page guard and API authz check only login state and role, so admin access is not blocked when 2FA is absent, contrary to the documented access policy.

nodes.label: Paid Stripe amount not bound to the ordered cart snapshot
nodes.rationale: Completion trusts any client-supplied Checkout Session, checks only PaymentIntent status, and rebuilds items from the mutable current cart, so a cheap payment can be converted into an expensive order.

nodes.label: Inventory validation incomplete and non-transactional
nodes.rationale: Quantity is never checked against stock_quantity except for an exact-zero test, and no path reserves or atomically decrements stock, so concurrent checkouts oversell and produce unfulfillable paid orders.

nodes.label: Unpublished items reachable through cart/wishlist/checkout
nodes.rationale: Service-role item lookups omit status='published', so posting a private item_id leaks name, price, image and category and can carry private goods into orders.

nodes.label: item-images bucket is fully public regardless of item status
nodes.rationale: public = true means draft and private product images are fetchable by URL, so publication control does not actually close at items.status; needs a private bucket with signed URLs or draft/published path separation.

nodes.label: Public API returns raw stock_quantity
nodes.rationale: UI only needs SOLD OUT / LOW STOCK, but the raw count lets unauthenticated clients estimate inventory levels for competitor research, hoarding bots and restock monitoring.

nodes.label: Public APIs expose status/created_at/updated_at
nodes.rationale: Internal operational fields let outsiders infer publication timing and update cadence; a public DTO should select only the minimum UI fields.

nodes.label: Request bodies and filters not schema-validated with Zod
nodes.rationale: Loosely typed quantity and free-form category/size/color/collection values flow straight into queries; not SQL injection, but a route to DB spam, cache pollution and inconsistent error paths.

nodes.label: Internal authorization error details returned to clients
nodes.rationale: authorizeAdminPermission returns err.message as details, leaking DB errors and internal configuration when the authz backend fails; client responses should be fixed strings with detail confined to server logs.

nodes.label: Contact PII stored in plaintext in audit_logs
nodes.rationale: The route inserts actor_email, detail, metadata.name and metadata.message directly rather than via logAudit, skipping the shared masking path; inquiries belong in a dedicated table with only an id and outcome in the audit log.

nodes.label: User-controlled limit without upper bound
nodes.rationale: The public news API accepts an unclamped limit; it should cap to a small maximum and require pagination beyond that.

nodes.label: Public complete endpoint accepts bank/cod without proof of payment
nodes.rationale: The schema still allows offline methods the UI never exposes, so anyone with a session_id cookie can submit unpaid orders, pollute the order table and clear carts.

nodes.label: Password reset breaks past the first 200 accounts
nodes.rationale: Both request and confirm resolve user_id by scanning listUsers({page:1,perPage:200}); beyond 200 users the token carries no user_id and confirm 404s, so a security change permanently breaks the account recovery path itself.

nodes.label: CSRF enforcement breaks the admin create-user UI
nodes.rationale: The API requires requireCsrfOrDeny but the page uses plain fetch without x-csrf-token, so authenticated admins get 403; admin tooling is also the recovery path, so the outage cost is high.

nodes.label: identify endpoint pre-creates email-confirmed users
nodes.rationale: serviceRole.auth.admin.createUser with email_confirm: true on arbitrary submitted addresses lets an unauthenticated caller create confirmed auth records for third-party emails; confirmation must follow proof of control.

nodes.label: Public POST endpoints lack Origin/Referer validation and bot defence
nodes.rationale: SameSite=Lax reduces classic CSRF but does not replace Origin checks, throttling or Turnstile/honeypot on cookie-authenticated public writes.

nodes.label: Third-party assets loaded globally in layout
nodes.rationale: Icon fonts and other third-party assets should be page-scoped and self-hosted or integrity-pinned rather than globally injected.

nodes.label: requireCsrfOrDeny
nodes.rationale: Double-submit CSRF gate already used by logout; reviews prescribe it as the standard control for cookie-authenticated mutations.

nodes.label: enforceRateLimit
nodes.rationale: Shared throttling helper the reviews repeatedly prescribe for public search, contact, cart, items and checkout routes.

nodes.label: authorizeAdminPermission
nodes.rationale: Prescribed replacement for shared-secret admin auth; must use DB ACL as final authority and add an MFA state check.

nodes.label: legacyPermissionMap
nodes.rationale: Token-role fallback map that grants admin.orders.manage to supporter and keeps stale roles authoritative.

nodes.label: logAudit
nodes.rationale: Shared audit helper carrying the masking path; bypassing it with direct audit_logs inserts loses redaction.

nodes.label: createServiceRoleClient
nodes.rationale: Reserve for operations that genuinely require elevated access; request-scoped authenticated clients should be used so DB policies remain active.

nodes.label: Row Level Security policy
nodes.rationale: The DB-side security boundary the reviews treat as the authoritative guardrail; deny-by-default policies must exist even when application code already filters.

nodes.label: HttpOnly secure cookie session storage
nodes.rationale: Prescribed replacement for localStorage token persistence; also how proxy.ts already stores cart session_id.

nodes.label: Stripe session/PaymentIntent metadata binding
nodes.rationale: Writing the cart session identifier into both Checkout Session and PaymentIntent metadata, then requiring both to match plus amount and currency, is the prescribed fix for cross-session payment reuse.

nodes.label: Immutable server-side checkout snapshot
nodes.rationale: Persisting a draft before redirecting to Stripe and finalizing only from that snapshot removes the mutable-cart window both complete and webhook paths currently rely on.

nodes.label: Private bucket with signed URL delivery
nodes.rationale: Prescribed fix for the fully public item-images bucket so asset availability follows publication state.

nodes.label: Aggregated stockState field
nodes.rationale: Return 'unknown' | 'out' | 'low' | 'in' publicly and keep exact counts to authorized admin APIs and server-side checkout.

nodes.label: src/lib/supabase/server.ts
nodes.rationale: Single most-cited file across the 2026-04-18 review set; lines 93 and 151-163 log cookie headers and decoded token values.

nodes.label: src/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts
nodes.rationale: Cited as the reference implementation of the requireCsrfOrDeny pattern other mutating routes should copy.

nodes.label: clientFetch
nodes.rationale: Should rely on same-origin cookies instead of extracting tokens from localStorage, and is the prescribed unification point for admin UI CSRF headers.

nodes.label: src/app/api/checkout/postal-code/route.ts
nodes.rationale: Public proxy with only a process-local memory cache, so multi-instance deployments do not dampen repeated upstream abuse.

nodes.label: src/app/api/webhook/stripe/route.ts
nodes.rationale: Signature verification correctly uses the raw body, but the handler rebuilds order_items from the live cart after payment_intent.succeeded.

nodes.label: src/proxy.ts
nodes.rationale: Applies CSP, Referrer-Policy, nosniff, DENY and HSTS, and stores cart session_id as an HttpOnly cookie.

nodes.label: src/lib/look/public.ts
nodes.rationale: Related-item lookup omits status='published', so an authenticated viewer session can pull unpublished product metadata through a public page path.

nodes.label: stripe_webhook_events
nodes.rationale: Stores raw Stripe payloads; RLS-protected for users but retention/redaction policy needs review because payloads carry customer metadata.

nodes.label: docs/3_ArchitectureDesign/hybrid-rbac.md
nodes.rationale: Defines the 'DB ACL as authority' model that admin-rbac.ts violates by accepting token role as an authorization source.

nodes.label: docs/4_DetailDesign/16_admin.md
nodes.rationale: Source of the admin audit, 2FA onboarding and refund-is-admin-only requirements the implementation misses.

nodes.label: docs/3_ArchitectureDesign/auth-structure.md
nodes.rationale: Defines the double-submit CSRF model that checkout and profile routes fail to apply.
